categories.main_business_segments: Exelon is a utility services holding company with six reportable segments: ComEd (Illinois), PECO (Pennsylvania), BGE (Maryland), Pepco (District of Columbia and Maryland), DPL (Delaware and Maryland), and ACE (New Jersey). Each segment engages in the purchase and regulated retail sale of electricity and/or natural gas, and transmission and distribution of these utilities to retail customers in their respective service territories.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company does not generate electricity; instead, it procures electricity through contracts and PJM-operated markets as directed by state laws and regulatory commissions. For natural gas, PECO, BGE, and DPL purchase supplies from multiple suppliers with firm transportation contracts and utilize storage facilities including LNG facilities, propane-air plants, and underground storage. The company operates transmission and distribution infrastructure including high-voltage electric transmission lines, distribution systems with overhead and underground lines, and natural gas pipelines.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Exelon serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers in six regulated utility service territories across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions. Primary markets include Northern Illinois (ComEd with 4.1 million customers), Southeastern Pennsylvania (PECO with 1.7 million customers), Central Maryland (BGE with 1.3 million customers), District of Columbia and Maryland (Pepco with 0.9 million customers), Delaware and Maryland (DPL with 0.5 million customers), and Southern New Jersey (ACE with 0.6 million customers).
categories.geographic_coverage: Exelon operates in six primary geographic regions: Northern Illinois including Chicago (ComEd), Southeastern Pennsylvania including Philadelphia (PECO), Central Maryland including Baltimore (BGE), District of Columbia and portions of Maryland (Pepco), portions of Delaware and Maryland (DPL), and portions of Southern New Jersey (ACE). The company serves a combined service territory population of approximately 22.5 million people across these regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Exelon operates in the midstream and downstream segments of the energy supply chain. The company owns and operates transmission and distribution infrastructure that delivers electricity and natural gas to end-use customers. It does not own generation assets (separated in February 2022) but procures electricity and natural gas from upstream suppliers and wholesalers for delivery to customers through its regulated distribution networks.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Exelon's strategy focuses on improving reliability and operations, enhancing customer experience, and advancing clean and affordable energy choices. Key initiatives include: investing approximately $31 billion over four years in infrastructure modernization including smart grid technology, storm hardening, and transmission projects; achieving a Path to Clean goal to reduce operations-driven GHG emissions 50% by 2030 and reach net zero by 2050; supporting customer energy efficiency programs with $3.5 billion in investments during 2023-2026; electrifying 30% of its vehicle fleet by 2025 and 50% by 2030; and exploring emerging clean energy technologies and decarbonization opportunities.
categories.revenue_model: Exelon generates revenue primarily through regulated utility rates for electricity and natural gas distribution and transmission services. Revenue is recognized when power and natural gas are physically delivered to customers, with unbilled revenue estimated monthly based on customer usage. The company also utilizes Alternative Revenue Program (ARP) accounting for formula rate mechanisms and revenue decoupling mechanisms that allow automatic rate adjustments. Additional revenues come from energy efficiency programs, transmission services, and recovery of regulatory program costs through approved riders and surcharges.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Exelon is a large regulated utility holding company operating in competitive and regulated markets. While the company's distribution and transmission operations are regulated monopolies in their service territories, it competes indirectly with other utilities and energy providers. Key competitors in the broader utility sector include PSEG and other regional utilities. Exelon's market position is strengthened by its scale, diversified geographic footprint across six states and Washington D.C., and its focus on operational excellence and regulatory relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Exelon is a large-cap utility company with significant financial scale. In 2022, Exelon reported net income attributable to common shareholders from continuing operations of $2,054 million (up from $1,616 million in 2021) and diluted earnings per share of $2.08 (up from $1.65 in 2021). The company has approximately 994 million shares outstanding and a market capitalization of approximately $44.5 billion as of August 2022. Exelon is classified as a large accelerated filer by the SEC and maintains investment-grade credit ratings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Exelon's value proposition centers on reliable, affordable energy delivery with a commitment to clean energy transition and customer service excellence. Key differentiators include: industry-leading operational excellence and reliability standards; significant investments in modernizing infrastructure to support grid resilience and clean energy integration; comprehensive energy efficiency and demand response programs; strong regulatory relationships and cost recovery mechanisms; commitment to environmental sustainability and GHG emissions reduction; and a diversified geographic footprint providing stability across multiple regulatory jurisdictions with complementary seasonal demand patterns.
